doc.title: Jason Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2025

title: A 2019 gig with Jerry Bergonzi at the Press Room
summary: Rowe asks about a conversation on stage; Palmer explains the setup and that Bergonzi taught him at NEC.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you about a particular gig and this is probably going to be tough because this was in 2019, and the video of it is online, a gig with Jerry Bergonzi, and you started out with “Stablemates.” No piano. I wonder if that probably was a choice, like you lay © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

out on the first tune. But there was a moment after that and you were going to play, you followed that with “All the Things You Are.” But there was a couple minutes where you and Jerry were like, put your heads together and you were having a conversation. And I think it was something to observe for students. Can you possibly recall what you were talking about? JP Oh you mean we were physically talking?

Yes. You were sort of facing the drummer. You weren’t addressing the audience. It’s almost like — I assumed it was like one of those things, “Okay here’s what we’re going to do, you play the first eight, I’ll do —” you know like you were doing an instant arrangement.

Yeah, yeah. We were playing up in Portsmouth at a place called the Press Room. We’ve done a few concerts, Jerry and I. Jerry was one of my teachers in college. One of the great artists of our time, one of the greatest tenor players ever. Great educator too. You know I took private lessons with him at NEC. Yeah I think at that moment we were either — for those gigs we didn’t have a set list, so we were either talking about how the tune we were playing was going to go or what we were going to play next. And yeah, that’s probably all that was. Yeah.
And then it happened. And then it sounded like it was, just like it was supposed to be.
That’s one of the great things about this music is that a little pre-planning can go a long way if people are being creative.
